sources.citation: Vansteenkiste, C. 1954. Review of B. J. Costermans, Mosaique Bangba (Bruxelles 1953). Kongo-Overzee 20(1): 84-86.
sources.note: Nothing; characterises Costermans 1953 as genealogical/ethnographic notes ('een enigszins losse verzameling van aantekeningen') with a dialect classification on pp. 30-31 and only incidental 'taalkundige aanduidingen' -- so the memoir itself is unlikely to contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: van Bulck, V. 1952. Taalstudie op de Bantoetaalgrens (Juni 1949-Jan. 1951) (International Bantu-Sudanese Team). Referaat, Commissie voor Afrikaanse Linguistiek, Tervuren 7 Dec. 1951. Kongo-Overzee 18(1): c. 36-49.
sources.note: No Bangba-specific statement. Generic remarks only: the team fixed 'de phonetische en tonetische transcriptie' in London before departure and notes 'de rol van de tonetiek zelfs in de intertribale verkeerstalen, om niet te spreken van al de niet-Bantoe- en Bantoetalen, die we te onderzoeken hadden'. Useful as a pointer that van Bulck's 1949-51 Bangba field data (450-500 nouns, grammatical questionnaire, tone-marked) exist and fed LSNBB vol. 1 (1956) and the RMCA linguistic archive.

sources.citation: van Bulck, Vaast. 1938. Die Ubangi-Uele-Sprachengruppe im nordlichen Belgisch-Kongo. Zeitschrift fur Ethnologie 70: 176-192.
sources.note: Nothing on tone or accent. Classification paper: reports the author's two ABangba word lists (Niangara and Dungu, 1932-33), establishes that Bangba groups with Mayogo, Bere (Czekanowski) and Mundu and is unrelated to the Bantu 'Pseudo-Bangba' (Mangbele, Bote, Mayenga, Mabadi); prints numerals 1-10 from five ABangba sources (Jacques, van der Kerken, van Bulck x2, Costermans) on pp. 189-190.

sources.citation: Czekanowski, Jan. 1924. Forschungen im Nil-Kongo-Zwischengebiet, Bd. 2: Ethnographie Uele/Ituri/Nil-Lander (Wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse der Deutschen Zentral-Afrika-Expedition 1907-1908, Bd. VI/2). Leipzig: Klinkhardt & Biermann. Anhang 'Sprachenaufnahmen', pp. 575-714; 'Kakwa, Mongwandi, Mayogu, Bere' table from p. 686.
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Bere' (= Bangba) list, 'ganz kurz gefasst', was recorded at Nala through interpreters; German-gloss vocabulary without accent or tone marks; the introduction discusses only informant reliability and classification by numerals.

sources.citation: Schultz, P. M. 1923-1924. Bangba-Fabeln und Erzahlungen. Anthropos 18-19: 386-419. (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description 'phonology or text collection' item for bang1345.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; interlinear fables only. More importantly the 'Bangba' of this article are NOT the Ubangian Bangba: Vorbemerkungen p. 386: 'Die Bangba.. gehoren zur grossen Klasse der Bantuneger. Sie sind ein Teil des Stammes, der von den Eingebornen als Babeo.., von den Europaern als Bangelima bezeichnet wird. Sie wohnen am Lohali-Fluss [Aruwimi].. von Yambuya aufwarts bis Panga' (texts are plainly Bantu: moto mokede, bangbele binyame). Glottolog's assignment of this text to bbe is a misattribution.
sources.venue: Anthropos 18-19: 386-419. (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description 'phonology or text collection' item for bang1345.)
